text:
alex: Heads-up — nightly kernel-smokecheck job just flagged a 30-40% p99 latency bump on ampere-midseq for seq_len=512 when the autotuner picked the 'vec4-opt' kernel. Looks like KV cache churn + small-batch path.
mira: ugh, saw that too. Is it consistent across runs or flaky?
alex: Reproduced locally on perf-lab-03 twice in a row. Attached microbench log: https://redwood.internal/perf/runs/4298765432
devon: can you paste the exact bench command you used?
alex: Sure —
```
./kbench --device ampere --model gpt-small --seq 512 --batch 1 --kernel-candidate vec4-opt --profile=timeline.json
```
sam: timeline shows repeated KV invalidates at token 128/256 boundaries, likely due to the kernel's prefetch stride not matching our KV slab layout.
perf-bot: perf-ci: kernel-smokecheck (4298765432) — regression detected: p99 up 38% vs baseline (4287654321).
mira: If kernel's memory access pattern thrashes the KV LRU then prefix caching benefits evaporate. Does the 'fallback' kernel avoid the same stride?
alex: fallback 'scalar-safe' is fine, p99 comparable to baseline. So autotuner picked vec4-opt for throughput win on longseq, but it backfired for midseq+small-batch combos.
devon: We need a fast triage: either add an arch-aware constraint (no vec4-opt on ampere for batch<=1 & seq<=1024), tweak autotuner scoring, or tweak the kernel to use contiguous KV layout.
sam: Quick suggestion: adjust autotuner scoring to penalize p99 regressions above 10% even if avg throughput improves. Might avoid these regressions slipping past gates.
mira: Agreed. Can we add a microprobe that exercises seq-length boundaries (e.g., 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024) with batch 1,2,4 to the smokecheck matrix tonight?
perf-bot: Action created: PERF-1189 — add seq-boundary matrix to kernel-smokecheck job.
alex: Also opening a kernel bug to track vec4-opt KV-stride: KERNEL-452. Moving candidate to gated=blocked for ampere-midseq until repro fixed.
devon: I'll own a quick perf patch to try aligning KV slab by 64 bytes in vec4-opt and re-run microbench. ETA today EOD.
sam: If devon needs a quick repro harness, use this snippet in the CI matrix:
```yaml
jobs:
  kernel-smokecheck-matrix:
    matrix:
      seq_len: [64,128,256,512,1024]
      batch: [1,2,4]
      device: [ampere, h100]
    steps:
      - run: ./kbench --device $device --seq $seq_len --batch $batch --profile=ci.json
```
mira: Good. Also add a post-step that diffs timeline.json for KV invalidate counts so the CI bot can auto-annotate if >5 invalidates.
perf-bot: Note: scheduling an expedited nightly run with the matrix variant at 02:15 UTC.
alex: Thanks — will follow up after devon lands a patch. If patch isn't ready by the rerun, we'll mute vec4-opt for ampere in the autotune candidates for now. :thumbsup:
mira: tagging @eng-oncall FYI in case this impacts prod (unlikely but better safe).
devon: Patch started: small alignment change pushed to my branch, running local microbench now. Will post results here.
sam: Perfect. Keep logs short — include timeline KV invalidate counts and p99 numbers only.
perf-bot: CI run started: kernel-smokecheck-matrix #4298765491
alex: closing loop: if the patch fixes p99 <5% regression, we can revert the temporary gating and update autotuner weights. Otherwise we keep vec4-opt excluded for this profile.
mira: cool, thanks everyone.
